name: Command Deck
narrativeOnEnter: The nerve centre of Meridian Station. Wide viewport looking out at open space — the rescue shuttle is clearly visible, holding position. Navigation terminals, captain's station, comms systems. A locked command locker sits against the far wall.

action.text:
CAPTAIN'S LOG — FINAL ENTRY

'Reactor alarm at 03:10. Ordered full crew evacuation — Kovalev stayed to attempt manual stabilisation. I should have ordered everyone off.

Distress beacon is active via the comms array — rescue shuttle is holding at 800m.
Escape pod launch code is 5519 — Kovalev and Chen both know it.

If anyone finds this log: stabilise the reactor first.
Then get to the pod bay. Then go home.

— Captain Diaz, Meridian Station Alpha'

Two shapes in the dark.

The closer one — 800 metres, running full lights — is MERIDIAN-3. Standard shuttle profile. It's been holding position for over an hour. Steady. Patient.

The farther one — 3 kilometres, running dark — is smaller. No lights, no transponder ping. But it's there. And twice, as you watch, it blinks.

Twice. Pause. Three times. Pause. Once.

Morse. W-E—A-R-E—H-E-R-E.

We are here.

They know someone's still aboard.
They're not moving.
They're waiting to see which ship you signal.

Through the external hull below the viewport: an access port. An external airlock — rarely used, but it connects directly to the docking ring. If the station's internal systems are compromised, that might be your backup route.

Navigation console for Meridian Station Alpha. Orbital positioning, thruster control, docking systems.

All systems showing nominal — the station's position is stable.

Two contacts on the proximity display:

CONTACT ALPHA — 'RESCUE SHUTTLE MERIDIAN-3 — HOLDING. AWAITING BEACON CONFIRMATION.'
Registered to: HELIOS GROUP (subsidiary charter)
Distance: 800m. Running standard lights. Crew complement: 4.

CONTACT BETA — UNKNOWN VESSEL
Registered to: [NO TRANSPONDER]
Distance: 3.1km. Running dark. Crew complement: unknown.
First detected: 03:08 GST — 6 minutes before station lockdown.

Someone has annotated the display in yellow grease pencil:

'Contact B = CALLISTO. Don't signal MERIDIAN-3.
HELIOS GROUP = AXIOM. They are NOT rescue.
Wait for Contact B. 148.350 MHz.'

The distress beacon is in the Comms Array.

hotspots.label: Lock Station & Signal All Clear
hotspots.lockedMessage: Reactor must be stabilised before you can lock the station down.
